sentences.text: The classic Tide Tables used on the exam have three main tables.
Table one gives the daily times and heights of high and low water at reference stations.
Table two lists subordinate stations, each tied to a reference station, with time differences for high and low water and height corrections.
Height corrections are either a number of feet to add or subtract, or a ratio, marked with an asterisk, that you multiply by the reference heights.
Table three lets you find the height of tide at any time between high and low water.
Times are in local standard time, so add one hour during daylight saving time.
